memory_update.text: POWL should be tracked as a direct electrical-distribution and switchgear candidate for AI data-center power infrastructure; key survival tests are data-center backlog repeatability, customer breadth, and margin conversion.

MOD should be tracked as a data-center cooling and liquid-cooling-adjacent candidate; key survival tests are Airedale order durability, customer concentration, capacity ramp, and data-center revenue disclosure.

IESC should be tracked as a skilled electrical/custom power-solutions implementation candidate; key survival tests are segment-level data-center exposure, backlog quality, labor availability, and project-margin risk.

The best public-market mapping for this node may have shifted from small-cap discovery to niche large-cap industrials that still carry non-AI industry labels. Future passes should search for sub-$10B suppliers beneath POWL/MOD/IESC: busway, enclosures, cable management, pumps, heat exchangers, commissioning, testing, and power-quality components.

node: Data-center power, thermal, and balance-of-plant infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expansion focused on second-order data-center infrastructure beneficiaries rather than GPU or hyperscaler leaders. The most relevant underfollowed lane is no longer purely small-cap: several names that used to screen as niche industrials have rerated into large-cap territory as data-center backlog became visible. The cleanest node exposures found in this pass are switchgear/power-control equipment, data-center thermal systems, and electrical/MEP execution capacity. These are not recommendations; they are candidates for deeper evidence work.
